findings.fix: Remove the orientation media query, or restyle #main-content so it reflows for portrait instead of being hidden entirely. If one specific widget genuinely requires landscape, scope the restriction to that widget alone and state why, leaving the rest of the content reachable in both orientations.
findings.violation: The page's own declared CSS hides the entire #main-content landmark, which holds the h1 and all three sections including the form, whenever the device reports portrait orientation, with no stated reason a single orientation is essential to this content. Unlike the criterion's own anchor examples, which describe one secondary widget losing reach in one orientation, this rule removes the page's whole substantive content for the default orientation most phone and tablet readers use, leaving only the header, nav, and footer reachable.

findings.evidence: AccessibilityFares and passes
findings.fix: Add a second, independent way to reach this page, such as a breadcrumb trail reflecting its place in the site, a site search form, or a sitemap link, so a reader arriving without prior knowledge of the navigation menu still has a path to it.
findings.location: #nav, <nav> element, the page's only navigation mechanism
findings.violation: The page exposes exactly one mechanism, the primary navigation menu in #nav, for a reader to locate it within the site; no search form, sitemap link, or breadcrumb trail is present anywhere in the document, and the page's own content does not mark it as one step in a linear process that would exempt it.

findings.fix: Set the field's autocomplete attribute to email, or the matching standard token for this input purpose.
findings.violation: This field's type, name, or id identifies the email input purpose, but it carries no autocomplete token, so the purpose is not programmatically determinable.

findings.fix: Remove outline:none, or replace it with a visible focus style such as a box-shadow or a 2px outline in a color meeting the 3:1 non-text contrast minimum against the surrounding background.
findings.violation: The inline style sets outline:none on this link with no replacement border, background, box-shadow, or outline declared anywhere else for it, so a keyboard user tabbing through the nav sees no visible change when this control receives focus.

findings.evidence: <div class="icon-delete" role="button" tabindex="0" aria-label="Delete item" id="s3-customcontrol" style="width:16px;height:16px">
findings.fix: Increase the control's rendered size to at least 24 by 24 CSS pixels, for example by adding padding around the icon, or keep the icon at its current visual size while enlarging the clickable hit area to 24 by 24 CSS pixels.
findings.location: #s3-customcontrol, <div role=button> control, accessible name 'Delete item', line 45
findings.violation: This pointer-operable custom control is sized 16 by 16 CSS pixels by its own inline style, below the 24 by 24 CSS pixel minimum, with no stated essential-size reason, no equivalent full-size control elsewhere on the page, no inline-text placement, and no spacing exception evident from the surrounding markup.

findings.fix: Add role=status (or aria-live=polite) to #s3-statuscard so assistive technology announces the confirmation text automatically when it appears, matching the live-region treatment already given to #s3-form-promo-error.
findings.location: #s3-statuscard, <div> status region, visible text 'Your changes are saved.', lines 41 to 43
findings.violation: This status confirmation region carries no role=status, role=alert, or aria-live attribute, so assistive technology does not announce it on its own once it appears; a screen-reader user is told nothing unless they happen to navigate back to this div afterward.
